title: Legends Untold - Illumination of Deepsorrow - New standalone campaign expansion (KS preview)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lbrq5ramx-A

Daniel (@dungeondive) previews The Illumination of Deepsorrow ahead of its Kickstarter. It's a standalone Legends Untold campaign that also expands the original Great Sewers and Weeping Caves novice sets. The game isn't simplified, but its presentation is revised, and the documentation is the headline. There's a how-to-play tutorial with its own card subset that walks two heroes through several full turns, a content almanac explaining every symbol, professionally printed flowcharts for each phase, a readiness tracker for light, pace and alertness, and a two-sided combat track for melee and ranged positioning.

The campaign has twelve scenarios. A successful run plays eight and branches toward one of two finales, depending on the clues found. Clue tracks for history, people and artifacts unlock lore passages, and failure moves the story forward instead of ending it. The new heroes include the Earthguide and the Envoy, who reminds him of Judge Dredd. He recaps the weapon-table combat using the battered axe's chart and admits he usually ignores the timer.

He wants more standalone scenarios or a roguelike endless mode, and pleads for the game to stay a big game in a small box, without the giant insert other crawls have grown. The Potions and Preparations add-on brings crafting from harvested herbs, minerals and monster parts, a layer he's open to despite wariness about the bookkeeping.

----

Daniel asks the series to stay a big game in a small box. Have you seen a game's box swell in later editions, and did it bother you?
